chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from al-'Amarki, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him).

He said: I asked him about a chicken, a pigeon, and birds similar to them that tread on excrement and then enter water from which wudu is to be performed for salat. He said: No, except if the water is abundant — a measure of a kurr of water.

key_terms.الْعَذِرَةَ: human excrement; a category of ritual impurity (najasah) in Islamic law
key_terms.كُرٍّ: kurr; a unit of water volume in Islamic jurisprudence at which water resists becoming ritually impure upon contact with najasah
key_terms.يُتَوَضَّأُ: wudu is performed; the ritual ablution required before salat

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling of Imam Musa al-Kadhim (AS) on performing wudu from water entered by birds that have walked through excrement?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam Musa al-Kadhim (AS), transmitted through his brother Ali ibn Ja'far, establishes a ruling on the ritual purity of water entered by birds that have stepped in human excrement. The Imam rules that wudu cannot be performed from such water unless it reaches the volume of a kurr — the minimum threshold in Shia fiqh at which water resists ritual contamination regardless of contact with a najis substance.
